messages:
maria: Heads-up — tenant 'Axiom' hit a big paging spike during their 3pm peak. Host shows ~65% GPU stalls from host->CPU faults. Can we give them transient prefetch priority to local NUMA staging so p95 latency stays under 120ms? logs: https://logs/axm/170981

sunil: Do we have a per-tenant staging priority API today? I thought we only have hint buckets. Not sure we have SLA semantics yet. :thinking:

maria: Not yet. Proposal sketch: soft-priority tokens tied to tenant + NUMA node with decay and a strict per-host budget. If budget exhausted, revert to best-effort prefetch. Avoid global evict thrash.

olivia: Sounds reasonable. API surface needs to be explicit: request = { tenant_id, numa_id, priority_level, budget_ms, decay_policy } and a server-side admission module that enforces fairness. Also we must ensure we don't starve other tenants.

jamal: Implementation note: prefer token-bucket per NUMA node rather than per-host. NUMA-local staging dramatically reduces cross-node copy latency. Example token config (rough):
```
prefetch_policy:
  tokens_per_min: 120
  burst: 30
  decay_window: 30s
```
This gives controlled bursts and automatic decay.

sunil: Also need an eviction safeguard: when premium prefetch increases resident set, the evictor should prefer demoting pages belonging to lower-tier tenants first. That requires tagging resident pages with tenant priority.

maria: Edge-case: large fragmented models. Aggressive prefetch can increase fragmentation in staging pools and actually hurt global throughput. We should add a fragmentation cap: max_staging_percent_per_tenant (e.g., 25%). If a tenant hits cap, downgrade prefetch tokens.

olivia: Agree. And we need observability: trace tokens -> prefetch hits -> tail latency improvement. Console should show token burn rate vs p50/p99 delta so SRE/product can judge ROI.

infra-bot: deploy queued: branch feature/numa-prefetch-sla -> staging at sha:abc123 :rocket:

jamal: QA plan: run multi-tenant synth load with mixes (many small models vs few huge models). Track: host_compaction_delta, prefetch_hit_ratio, p99_latency, staging_fragmentation. Auto-throttle rule: if compaction_delta > 15% in 5m window, reduce token allotment by 50% for offending tenant.

maria: Also add a fast-path for explicit enterprise SLA: Dedicated tenants can opt-in to guaranteed prefetch (higher budget) at contract time, but still bounded to prevent OOM cascade.

sunil: One more: we should avoid changing core allocator contracts. Keep token admission in the staging controller layer so allocator interfaces remain stable. That reduces blast radius.

olivia: Yep — controller-layer enforcement + allocator only needs minor tagging hooks (tenant_id, priority). Keep eviction policies pluggable.

maria: I'll draft an RFC today covering: API payloads, token-bucket semantics, fragmentation cap, eviction priority mapping, telemetry, and rollout plan (staging then canary). Will ping reviewers @sunil @jamal @olivia. :thumbsup:

olivia: Thanks — will review.

jamal: ack, will add compaction telemetry dashboards to the QA checklist.

maria: Cool. If no major blockers I want to prototype this week.
